name: Healthcare
summary: Appointment reminders, waitlist fill, intake, eligibility checks, referrals, and recalls.

automations.title: Front Desk Daily Briefing & Schedule Gap Alert
automations.summary: Each morning before the office opens, the office manager and front desk team receive an automated briefing: today's confirmed appointments, patients…
steps: Each morning before the office opens, the office manager and front desk team receive an automated briefing: today's confirmed appointments, patients who haven't confirmed, the day's unscheduled gaps, and any outstanding patient balances over a set threshold.
Unconfirmed appointments trigger an automated text asking the patient to confirm or reschedule.

Schedule gaps that appear during the day are automatically pushed to a waitlist outreach sequence so that cancellations are filled before the slot goes empty, and the front desk team starts every single day fully informed rather than discovering problems as they arrive.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a medical office manager spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Kareo or SimplePractice)

automations.title: Referral Tracking & Specialist Follow-Up System
automations.summary: When a provider refers a patient to a specialist, this automation logs the referral with the patient name, specialist, diagnosis code, and urgency…
steps: When a provider refers a patient to a specialist, this automation logs the referral with the patient name, specialist, diagnosis code, and urgency level, sends the referral packet to the specialist office automatically, and texts the patient their specialist's contact information with instructions to schedule.

If confirmation that the appointment was booked hasn't been received within seven days, a follow-up task is created and the patient receives another reminder, closing the referral loop that typically gets lost the moment the patient walks out the door.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a patient care coordinator re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something.
tools: EHR with API access (e.g., athenahealth or eClinicalWorks)
Airtable or Google Sheets (referral tracking log)

automations.title: Eligibility Verification & Prior Authorization Tracker
automations.summary: For every appointment scheduled more than 48 hours out, this automation automatically verifies the patient's insurance eligibility and pulls their…
steps: For every appointment scheduled more than 48 hours out, this automation automatically verifies the patient's insurance eligibility and pulls their current deductible and copay information, flagging any coverage discrepancies before the patient arrives.

Procedures that require prior authorization are identified from the appointment type, a pre-auth request is initiated automatically, and the status is tracked daily until approved, ensuring no one discovers a missing auth after a procedure has already been performed, which is when it becomes a write-off instead of a payment.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a medical billing specialist is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Clearinghouse with eligibility API (e.g., Availity or Change Healthcare)

automations.title: Staff Credentialing & License Expiration Tracker
automations.summary: Every provider and licensed staff member's credentials (DEA license, state medical license, malpractice insurance, BLS certification, and board…
steps: Every provider and licensed staff member's credentials (DEA license, state medical license, malpractice insurance, BLS certification, and board certifications) are tracked with expiration dates in a central system.

Renewal reminders are sent to the staff member at 120, 60, and 30 days before expiration, and the practice administrator receives a weekly compliance dashboard showing every credential status across the entire practice.
Any credential that lapses without a renewal on file triggers an immediate escalation, because an expired license is a compliance and liability issue that cannot wait until the next Friday report.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a practice administrator spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Email or Slack (staff renewal reminders and admin escalations)

automations.title: Session Notes Reminder & Insurance Billing Trigger
automations.summary: Each time a session is marked complete in the calendar, the therapist receives an automated prompt to finalize their session notes within 24 hours.
steps: Each time a session is marked complete in the calendar, the therapist receives an automated prompt to finalize their session notes within 24 hours.

Once notes are locked, the system automatically pushes the superbill or CMS-1500 data to the clearinghouse for billing, keeping the provider compliant with documentation standards and ensuring no session slips through the billing cycle unbilled.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, a therapist / mental health provider has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: EHR/practice management software (e.g., SimplePractice or TherapyNotes)

automations.title: Appointment Reminder & Confirmation System
automations.summary: Every scheduled appointment triggers an automated reminder sequence: a text and email 72 hours out, a second text 24 hours out, and a final same-day…
steps: Every scheduled appointment triggers an automated reminder sequence: a text and email 72 hours out, a second text 24 hours out, and a final same-day nudge two hours before arrival.

Each message includes a one-tap link that lets the patient confirm, reschedule, or cancel without ever calling the office, and every response updates the schedule in real time so the front desk coordinator sees the day's true status at a glance.
Patients who don't respond to the 24-hour reminder are automatically flagged for a personal call before the slot is written off.

Practices running this system typically cut no-show rates by 30 to 40 percent within the first two months, turning a schedule full of unconfirmed guesses into one the front desk can actually plan around.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, a front desk coordinator spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Kareo or SimplePractice)

automations.title: New Patient Intake & EHR Sync System
automations.summary: As soon as a new patient books their first appointment, this automation sends a secure digital intake packet 48 hours ahead of the visit, covering…
steps: As soon as a new patient books their first appointment, this automation sends a secure digital intake packet 48 hours ahead of the visit, covering demographics, insurance details, medical history, and consent forms.

Completed forms are parsed automatically and written directly into the correct fields in the EHR, so the new patient coordinator opens the chart on visit day already populated rather than handing the patient a clipboard at the front desk.
Patients who haven't completed the packet by 24 hours before their visit receive an automatic reminder text with a direct link to finish it.
First-visit check-in time typically drops from 15 minutes of paperwork to under 3 minutes of verification, and the provider walks into the room with a complete history instead of a blank chart.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a new patient coordinator re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: EHR with API access (e.g., athenahealth or DrChrono)

automations.title: Recall & Preventive Care Reminder System
automations.summary: This automation scans the patient roster daily against each patient's last visit date and the recommended interval for their care type, whether…
steps: This automation scans the patient roster daily against each patient's last visit date and the recommended interval for their care type, whether that's an annual physical, a six-month cleaning, or a mammogram screening, and automatically queues a reminder message once a patient crosses that threshold.

A first message goes out by email at the 11-month mark, followed by a text at 12 months, and a final personal outreach task assigned to the recall coordinator if the patient hasn't booked by 13 months.
Every message includes a direct scheduling link so the patient can book in two taps instead of waiting on hold.
Practices that turn this on typically recover 20 to 25 percent of patients who would otherwise have quietly lapsed out of the practice.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a patient recall coordinator has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks.
tools: EHR or practice management software (e.g., eClinicalWorks or Kareo)

automations.title: Automated Insurance Verification Pre-Check
automations.summary: Exactly 48 hours before every scheduled appointment, this automation pings the payer's eligibility API directly through the clearinghouse and pulls…
steps: Exactly 48 hours before every scheduled appointment, this automation pings the payer's eligibility API directly through the clearinghouse and pulls back the patient's active coverage status, plan type, and copay amount.

Appointments that come back with inactive coverage, a terminated plan, or a mismatch between the patient's stated insurance and what's on file are flagged immediately to the front office team, giving staff a full day and a half to reach the patient before they show up expecting a visit their insurance won't cover.
Clean verifications are logged silently so no one wastes time double-checking coverage that's already confirmed.
Front offices using this catch coverage problems before the visit instead of during checkout, when the only options left are an awkward conversation or an unpaid claim.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, a patient access representative spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Clearinghouse with eligibility API (e.g., Availity or Change Healthcare)

automations.title: Post-Visit Care Instruction Automation
automations.summary: The moment a visit is marked complete in the schedule, this automation matches the visit type, whether it's a wellness check, a minor procedure, or…
steps: The moment a visit is marked complete in the schedule, this automation matches the visit type, whether it's a wellness check, a minor procedure, or a chronic care follow-up, against a library of pre-approved care instructions and sends the corresponding summary to the patient by text and email within minutes of checkout.
Instructions include medication timing, activity restrictions, and a clear list of symptoms that warrant a call back to the office.
Patients discharged after a procedure receive a follow-up check-in message 48 hours later asking how they're recovering, with any concerning response routed straight to the clinical care coordinator.
Offices report meaningfully fewer same-day callback questions once patients leave with clear, visit-specific instructions instead of a generic printed sheet.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a clinical care coordinator, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: EHR with API access (e.g., athenahealth or eClinicalWorks)

automations.title: HIPAA-Safe Patient Review Request System
automations.summary: Three days after a completed visit, this automation sends a short review request that references only the fact that the patient visited the…
steps: Three days after a completed visit, this automation sends a short review request that references only the fact that the patient visited the practice, never the reason for the visit, the diagnosis, or any treatment detail, keeping the message fully clear of protected health information.
The request only goes out to patients who have an active consent to be contacted on file, and it automatically excludes anyone flagged as a sensitive or high-risk case.

Patients who respond positively are routed to a public review link for Google or Healthgrades, while anyone who indicates dissatisfaction is routed privately to the patient experience coordinator instead of a public platform.
Practices using this approach see review volume climb steadily without ever putting a compliance officer at risk.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a patient experience coordinator spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Podium or BirdEye (review routing and publishing)

automations.title: Telehealth Link Automation
automations.summary: When a telehealth visit is booked, this automation immediately generates a unique, secure video link through the practice's HIPAA-compliant platform…
steps: When a telehealth visit is booked, this automation immediately generates a unique, secure video link through the practice's HIPAA-compliant platform and sends it to the patient by email along with a calendar invite.
A second reminder text goes out 15 minutes before the appointment with the same link and a one-line tech-check prompt, so patients aren't scrambling to find the email at the last minute.
Providers receive their own link automatically loaded into their daily schedule view, with no separate login step required.
No-shows on virtual visits, which tend to run higher than in-person appointments, typically drop by half once patients have a link in hand at exactly the moment they need it.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a telehealth coordinator manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: HIPAA-compliant telehealth platform (e.g., Doxy.me or Zoom for Healthcare)

automations.title: Cancellation Waitlist Fill System
automations.summary: The moment an appointment is canceled, this automation checks the waitlist for that provider and appointment type, ranks patients by how long…
steps: The moment an appointment is canceled, this automation checks the waitlist for that provider and appointment type, ranks patients by how long they've been waiting and their stated availability, and texts the top match with the open slot and a 10-minute window to claim it with a single reply.
If there's no response in 10 minutes, the offer automatically cascades to the next patient on the list, continuing until the slot is filled or the list is exhausted.
The scheduling coordinator sees the entire cascade and final outcome logged in one place, with no manual calling down a paper list required.
Practices running this typically fill same-day cancellations that used to sit open for the rest of the day within 20 minutes of the cancellation itself.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a scheduling coordinator, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Kareo or SimplePractice)

automations.title: Multi-Touch Appointment Reminder & Confirmation Sequence
automations.summary: Every time an appointment is booked in the practice management system, this automation enrolls the patient in a multi-touch reminder sequence: an…
steps: Every time an appointment is booked in the practice management system, this automation enrolls the patient in a multi-touch reminder sequence: an email confirmation the moment the visit is scheduled, a text 48 hours out, a second text 24 hours out, and a final same-day nudge two hours before arrival.

Each message carries a one-tap link so the patient can confirm, reschedule, or cancel without tying up the phone lines, and every response writes straight back into the schedule through Zapier so the front desk always sees accurate, real-time status.
Patients who ignore both the 48- and 24-hour texts are automatically flagged for a personal callback before the slot is treated as confirmed.

Practices running this sequence typically see front-desk call volume drop by a third within the first month, freeing staff to handle patients standing in front of them instead of chasing confirmations over the phone.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, a patient communications manager has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Kareo or SimplePractice)

automations.title: No-Show Recovery & Rebooking Sequence
automations.summary: The instant a scheduled visit is marked as a no-show in the practice management system, this automation fires a re-engagement text within minutes…
steps: The instant a scheduled visit is marked as a no-show in the practice management system, this automation fires a re-engagement text within minutes, acknowledging the missed appointment without blame and offering a direct link to rebook the next available slot.

If the patient hasn't rebooked within 24 hours, a follow-up email goes out with two or three specific open times pulled live from the schedule, and patients who no-show twice in a rolling 12-month window are automatically flagged to the revenue cycle manager for a personal outreach call before a no-show fee policy kicks in.
Every recovered visit and every fee applied is logged automatically in a shared tracker so leadership can see the real dollar impact of missed appointments.
Practices running this typically recover 15 to 20 percent of no-show visits that would otherwise have simply vanished from the schedule.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a revenue cycle manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it.

automations.title: New Patient Intake Forms & Insurance Pre-Collection
automations.summary: The moment a new patient books their first visit online, this automation immediately sends a secure digital intake packet covering demographics…
steps: The moment a new patient books their first visit online, this automation immediately sends a secure digital intake packet covering demographics, medical history, and a photo upload request for the front and back of the insurance card.
As soon as the card images come back, the intake specialist gets a notification to key the coverage into the practice management system ahead of the visit instead of scrambling at check-in.

Patients who haven't completed the packet by 24 hours before their appointment automatically receive a reminder text with a direct link to finish it, and any patient who submits an insurance card that doesn't match an active plan on file is flagged for a pre-visit call.
First-visit paperwork time typically drops from 15 minutes in the waiting room to a few minutes of verification at the desk.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, an intake specialist is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Booking-Triggered Insurance Eligibility Pre-Check
automations.summary: As soon as a patient books an appointment online or by phone, this automation automatically pings the practice's clearinghouse to run an eligibility…
steps: As soon as a patient books an appointment online or by phone, this automation automatically pings the practice's clearinghouse to run an eligibility check against the insurance information on file, pulling back plan status, deductible remaining, and copay amount within seconds.

Appointments that come back with inactive coverage or a plan mismatch are flagged immediately in a shared queue the front office supervisor reviews each morning, giving staff time to reach the patient before the visit instead of discovering a coverage gap at checkout.
Clean checks are logged silently so no one wastes time re-verifying coverage that's already confirmed.
Front offices running this catch the majority of coverage problems days before the patient ever walks in, instead of finding out during an awkward conversation at the counter.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a front office supervisor is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Post-Visit Satisfaction Survey & Alert Routing
automations.summary: Within a few hours of every completed visit, this automation sends the patient a short two-question satisfaction survey by text or email asking how…
steps: Within a few hours of every completed visit, this automation sends the patient a short two-question satisfaction survey by text or email asking how the visit went and whether anything needs follow-up.

Responses that score below a set threshold are routed instantly to the quality improvement coordinator as an internal alert, complete with the patient's name and visit details, so a staff member can call back the same day before a frustrated patient leaves a public review instead.
Responses that score high automatically prompt a follow-up message inviting the patient to leave a Google review, keeping the two paths completely separate.
Practices running this typically catch and resolve the majority of service issues privately, well before they would have otherwise shown up online.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a quality improvement coordinator, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: Preventive Care Recall Reminder Automation
automations.summary: Each night, this automation scans the patient roster against the recommended interval for annual physicals, cleanings, and standard screenings, and…
steps: Each night, this automation scans the patient roster against the recommended interval for annual physicals, cleanings, and standard screenings, and automatically queues an outreach message for anyone who has crossed their due date without a visit on the books.

A first reminder goes out by email, a follow-up text arrives a week later if the patient hasn't scheduled, and any patient still unbooked after 30 days is handed to the wellness program coordinator as a personal outreach task.
Every message includes a direct scheduling link so the patient can book in two taps rather than sitting on hold.
Practices that turn this recall system on typically bring back a meaningful share of patients who would otherwise have quietly drifted out of the preventive care cycle entirely.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a wellness program coordinator handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: EHR or practice management software (e.g., eClinicalWorks or Kareo)

automations.title: Prescription Refill Request Routing & Status Updates
automations.summary: When a patient submits a refill request through the online form, this automation automatically routes it to the correct provider's queue based on…
steps: When a patient submits a refill request through the online form, this automation automatically routes it to the correct provider's queue based on the medication and prescribing physician, and immediately sends the patient a confirmation that the request was received.

As the request moves from submitted to provider review to approved, an automatic status text keeps the patient updated at each stage, and once the provider approves it, the request is transmitted to the pharmacy through the practice's e-prescribing system without a medical assistant having to manually relay the approval by phone.
Requests still sitting in the queue after 24 hours automatically escalate to a reminder for the assigned provider.
Refill turnaround time typically drops from a day or more of phone tag to just a few hours.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a medical assistant spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: EHR with e-prescribing (e.g., athenahealth or RXNT)

automations.title: Cancellation Waitlist Auto-Fill Texting System
automations.summary: The moment an appointment is canceled in the schedule, this automation automatically texts the next patient on the waitlist for that provider and…
steps: The moment an appointment is canceled in the schedule, this automation automatically texts the next patient on the waitlist for that provider and visit type, offering the newly open slot on a strict first-come, first-served basis with a short window to claim it.
If there's no reply within 10 minutes, the offer cascades automatically to the next patient on the list, continuing down the queue until someone claims the slot or the list runs out.
The office manager sees the full cascade and outcome logged automatically, with no one manually working a paper waitlist by phone.
Same-day cancellations that used to sit open for the rest of the day typically get refilled within 20 minutes of the original cancellation.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means an office manager handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.summary: As soon as a telehealth visit is booked, this automation generates a unique, secure video link through the practice's HIPAA-compliant platform and…
steps: As soon as a telehealth visit is booked, this automation generates a unique, secure video link through the practice's HIPAA-compliant platform and sends it to the patient immediately by email along with a calendar invite.

A set number of minutes before the appointment, a second reminder text goes out with the same link and a one-line prompt to test camera and microphone access ahead of time, so patients aren't troubleshooting connectivity while the provider waits.
The virtual care coordinator's dashboard shows link-delivery and confirmation status for every visit on the day's telehealth schedule.
Practices using this typically see virtual no-show rates drop by half once patients have a working link in hand at exactly the right moment.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a virtual care coordinator is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: HIPAA-compliant telehealth platform (e.g., Doxy.me or Zoom for Healthcare)

automations.title: New Patient Welcome & Orientation Sequence
automations.summary: Booking a first appointment automatically enrolls the new patient in a multi-touch welcome series managed by the patient engagement specialist: an…
steps: Booking a first appointment automatically enrolls the new patient in a multi-touch welcome series managed by the patient engagement specialist: an initial email covering clinic policies and what to expect at the first visit, a second message a few days later walking through patient portal setup, and a third message answering the most common new-patient questions about parking, paperwork, and insurance.
Patients who haven't activated their portal account by the time of their visit get an extra nudge with a direct setup link.
The sequence pauses automatically once the first visit is completed, replaced by the practice's standard post-visit communications.
New patients arrive already familiar with how the office runs, cutting first-visit confusion and the repetitive questions front desk staff used to field every single day.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, a patient engagement specialist spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work.

automations.title: Lab Result Ready Notification System
automations.summary: The moment new lab results are uploaded and finalized in the system, this automation automatically sends the patient a portal notification and a…
steps: The moment new lab results are uploaded and finalized in the system, this automation automatically sends the patient a portal notification and a text letting them know results are available, along with a brief note on whether they should expect a call from the office or can simply review the results themselves online.

Results flagged by the provider as needing discussion automatically route to the clinical support specialist's task queue for a callback, while routine normal results are released to the patient portal without staff intervention.
Patients who haven't logged in to view flagged results within 48 hours trigger an automatic reminder text.
This keeps patients informed the moment results land instead of waiting on a callback queue, while making sure nothing that needs a conversation slips through unnoticed.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a clinical support specialist has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: EHR with API access (e.g., athenahealth or eClinicalWorks)

automations.title: Referral Authorization Turnaround Tracking
automations.summary: Once a specialist referral requiring prior authorization is logged, this automation automatically starts a turnaround clock against the payer's…
steps: Once a specialist referral requiring prior authorization is logged, this automation automatically starts a turnaround clock against the payer's expected processing window and checks the authorization status daily through the clearinghouse.

If an authorization is still pending once it passes the expected turnaround time, an alert routes directly to the prior authorization specialist with the payer, patient, and days-pending clearly listed, so a staff member can call the payer before the delay pushes into the patient's scheduled visit date.
Approved authorizations are logged automatically and attached to the referral record, and the referring provider's office receives a status update without anyone needing to call and ask.
Practices using this catch stalled authorizations days earlier than manual spreadsheet tracking ever did.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, a prior authorization specialist spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Clearinghouse with prior authorization tracking (e.g., Availity)

automations.title: Patient Portal Registration Nudge Sequence
automations.summary: Patients who complete a visit without activating their online portal account are automatically enrolled in a short nudge sequence managed by the…
steps: Patients who complete a visit without activating their online portal account are automatically enrolled in a short nudge sequence managed by the patient portal administrator: a first email with a direct setup link sent a few days after the visit, a follow-up text a week later if the account is still inactive, and a final reminder attached to their next appointment confirmation.
Once a patient activates their account, they're automatically removed from the sequence so no one keeps getting nudged after signing up.
The portal administrator gets a weekly report showing overall activation rate by provider, making it easy to see where extra front-desk encouragement is still needed.
Portal adoption typically climbs substantially within a few months without staff manually calling a single patient.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a patient portal administrator handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Chronic Care Management Check-In Automation
automations.summary: Patients enrolled in a chronic care management program are automatically placed on a scheduled check-in cadence between visits, receiving a brief…
steps: Patients enrolled in a chronic care management program are automatically placed on a scheduled check-in cadence between visits, receiving a brief text or portal message asking them to report how they're feeling, whether medications are being taken as prescribed, and whether any new symptoms have come up.

Responses that indicate a concerning symptom or a missed medication are routed immediately to the chronic care manager for same-day follow-up, while routine check-ins are logged automatically to the patient's chart for the next visit.
The system also tracks total time spent on care management activities, which the practice needs for accurate CCM billing each month.
Patients get more consistent touchpoints between visits, and the chronic care manager spends time on the patients who actually need it instead of chasing down status on everyone.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a chronic care manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: EHR with API access (e.g., athenahealth or eClinicalWorks)

automations.title: Outstanding Balance Payment Reminder Sequence
automations.summary: Once a patient's account carries an outstanding balance past the insurance adjustment period, this automation automatically enrolls them in a…
steps: Once a patient's account carries an outstanding balance past the insurance adjustment period, this automation automatically enrolls them in a payment reminder sequence: a friendly email statement with a direct online payment link at 15 days past due, a text reminder at 30 days, and a final notice at 45 days before the account is flagged for the billing coordinator's manual review.
Every payment made through the link automatically updates the balance and removes the patient from the sequence, so no one keeps getting reminded after they've already paid.
Balances that remain unpaid past 60 days are automatically compiled into a weekly aging report for the billing coordinator.
Practices running this typically collect a meaningfully higher share of outstanding balances without adding a single hour of manual billing follow-up calls.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a billing coordinator, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Payment processor (e.g., Stripe or a patient payment portal)

automations.title: Provider Unavailability Auto-Reschedule Alert
automations.summary: When a provider is marked unavailable for a day, whether from illness, an emergency, or a schedule change, this automation immediately pulls every…
steps: When a provider is marked unavailable for a day, whether from illness, an emergency, or a schedule change, this automation immediately pulls every affected appointment for that day and automatically flags each patient's booking for rescheduling.

Each affected patient receives a text or email within minutes offering two or three of the next available slots with that provider or a covering provider, with a direct link to pick a new time in one tap.
The scheduling supervisor gets a real-time dashboard showing how many of the day's affected patients have already rebooked versus still need a personal call.
What used to be an hour of front-desk staff manually calling down a printed schedule now resolves itself for the majority of patients before the office even opens.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a scheduling supervisor, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Kareo or SimplePractice)

automations.title: Immunization Due Date Reminder System
automations.summary: Based on each patient's date of birth and the standard immunization schedule, this automation automatically identifies children and adults who have…
steps: Based on each patient's date of birth and the standard immunization schedule, this automation automatically identifies children and adults who have a vaccine coming due and sends the parent or patient a reminder by text and email with the specific vaccine name and the recommended visit window.

Reminders go out 30 days ahead of the due date with a second nudge at 7 days if no appointment has been booked, and the pediatric care coordinator receives a weekly summary of which patients remain unscheduled for follow-up outreach.
Reminders automatically stop once the immunization is logged as administered in the chart, so no one receives a nudge for a shot they've already had.
Practices running this see immunization compliance climb steadily without staff manually reviewing charts each week to find who's due.
